dialect.guess: GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) / ORCA project (JMA Japan Medical Association)
evidence: IDENTIFICATION DIVISION / ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / DATA DIVISION / PROCEDURE DIVISION all present
LINKAGE SECTION with USING clause on PROCEDURE DIVISION

purpose.summary: This program is part of the ORCA JMA (Japan Medical Association) standard medical receipt software. It handles the 'self-clinic code expiry date change' (自院コード期限切れ変更) screen (Z07), managing point/fee master (tensu master) records whose validity periods have expired. It initialises screen areas, retrieves tensu master records from a database via MCP calls, and drives screen navigation and data entry for updating expiry dates.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical billing (Japanese medical receipt processing)

notable_features: No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — uses proprietary MCP (Message Control Program) database access via CALL 'ORCMCPSUB'
Heavy use of COPY copybooks (.INC files) for screen layouts, file records, and subroutine parameter areas
Japanese text in comments (encoded as latin-1/EUC-JP mixed, explaining the garbled characters)
LINKAGE SECTION with multiple passed areas (MCPAREA, SPAAREA, LINKAREA, SCRAREA)
24 CALL statements to various ORCA utility subprograms (ORCSDAY, ORCMCPSUB, etc.)
EVALUATE with ALSO clause for multi-condition dispatch
SPA (Screen Parameter Area) pattern typical of ORCA/OpenCOBOL screen management
No COMP-3 usage despite being a production system
verdict.notes: The file is encoded in EUC-JP (Japanese) but was decoded as latin-1, causing the Japanese comment text to appear as garbled latin-1 characters. The program is clearly part of the well-known open-source ORCA medical receipt system developed by JMA Japan. The 'online-cics' program_type label is used loosely — ORCA uses its own MCP windowing/screen framework rather than CICS, but the pattern (screen-driven, linkage-based, SPA state management) is functionally equivalent to an online transaction program.
